title: test-0134-GEN-PHONES
passage: In the bustling city of Bengaluru, residents recently raised concerns about a new mobile tower installed near a local school. Many parents feared that the tower’s radio waves would cause health issues for their children. However, experts from the Department of Telecommunications clarified that mobile towers emit non-ionising radiation, which is fundamentally different from the high-energy ionising radiation found in nuclear materials. Unlike nuclear radiation, which can damage DNA, radio waves from phones and towers lack the energy to break chemical bonds in human cells. Furthermore, experts explained that phone heat is simply a result of the battery working hard, not a sign of dangerous radiation. To keep eyes healthy, students were advised to follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. This is much more effective than taking one long break after hours of screen time. Finally, the experts reminded everyone that using a certified, original charger is essential, as cheap, uncertified chargers may lack safety features that prevent overheating. Radio waves travel through space at the speed of light, not like sound, and they do not linger in the body after a call ends. By understanding these facts, we can use technology safely without unnecessary fear.
